parts.text:

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Reaction 1 is an oxidation reaction.

Identify the reagent(s) and conditions for reaction 1.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
$\mathbf{A}$, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{CCO}_2\text{H}$, is a solid at room temperature.

$\mathbf{B}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{(CH}_2\text{)}_2\text{CH}_3$, is an isomer of $\mathbf{A}$. $\mathbf{B}$ is a liquid at room temperature.

Explain the difference in the physical states of $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$, with reference to any intermolecular forces that may exist.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Give the balanced equation for the reaction of $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{CCHO}$ with $\text{NaBH}_4$ to form $\mathbf{S}$.

Use $[\text{H}]$ to represent an atom of hydrogen provided by $\text{NaBH}_4$.

parts.label: (c)(vii)
parts.text:
$\mathbf{X}$ contains a carbonyl group. $\mathbf{X}$ reacts with $\text{HCN}$, in the presence of a small amount of $\text{NaCN}$, to form $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{C(OH)CN}$ as shown.

$$\mathbf{X} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{C(OH)CN}$$

Draw the mechanism of the reaction of $\mathbf{X}$ with $\text{HCN}$.

- Draw the structure of $\mathbf{X}$ and the intermediate.
- Include all charges, partial charges, lone pairs and curly arrows.
